title: Opinion on some best practices for Astra usage (this may also apply to Claude)
author: AsparagusOk8818
selftext:
...I can't think of a reason this would not work with Claude, but I haven't tried Claude (yet), so I don't know for sure. 



So, I think this might not be useful advice for a lot of people here, but in case you are like me and got used to a certain style of workflow because you've been using GPT models for a little while and got used to certain quirks/patterns of behaviour, this post might be helpful to you.

  
(Also please note that I do not at all claim to know how to 'token maxx' this method works for me; it may be token inefficient. If you are worried about squeezing every single last possible drop out of your token budget, that's totally understandable; you won't find that here unless it is purely by chance)

If you have been doing this: 

 \- Manually build definition files and data structures.   
 \- Tell GPT to use that as context and build the logic modules to fill in the blanks, because that's just how things needed to go before.  
 \- Manually plan/build out lists of placeholder fluff 

  
...This is not the best way to use Astra. If you enjoy the manual editing, hey, have at it. But Astra is both much faster and more token-efficient if you ask it to just plan everything; let it build the definition files itself, let it create the placeholder fluff and starting values, etc etc. 

  
Here's an example Astra prompt, to get a sense of the workflow within the LLM's chat interface for me: 

  
*Perfect, thank you.*

*Can we please plan the implementation of a shotgun weapon currency, shotgun shell ammunition, and some environmental storage containers?*

*The shotgun should be a 1 x 3 piercing ranged weapon with a range of 6, a damage value of 5, a fatigue value of 1, an attack delay of 2 and requiring consumption of shotgun shell ammunition to be used (ranged weapons and ammunition usage is not yet established in the game and requires new implementation).*

*shotgun shells should be 1 x 2 currency with an ammunition pool of 12*

*I'd also like to ideally change the existing storage rack fixture to be actual storage containers that we could put shotguns and shotgun shells into. Could you recommend a means of doing that that would mesh with the game's existing systems?*

  
*Do not implement anything yet, this is just planning / discussion.*

  
Note that you do need to instruct the LLM during planning not to implement anything, because otherwise it ain't got no brakes on the train.

  
Astra will then produce a detailed plan and ask you to fill in any context or ambiguities. Answer those questions. Once that's done:   


*That sounds great; Could you please implement that?*

*If you have any questions or require clarification, please ask either before or during implementation. Please create any additional modules you feel would be useful to have for this implementation, but only if they are needed.*

  
Do you have to be polite? Probably not. But I choose to be. 

Asking for clarifications is important, because otherwise the model can and will make a bunch of assumptions about systems that will later need to be undone. 

Asking it to create modules if it needs to prevents it from just choosing one file and letting her rip and clogging it with all of the code for a billion different systems.

  


As a general rule, the bigger the chunk of your project that Astra can work on per prompt, the more efficient the token usage. But the bigger the chunk it works on per prompt, the more it will warp the work. So you have to get a feel for the trade-off between getting human-readable and editable code vs. LLM spaghetti code, where token usage and personal work are effectively spent to get cleaner code. 

  
If you haven't yet switched away from the machine just being a gap-filler to treating it as a plan-and-execute collaborative engine, you probably should do that. It's a night-and-day difference (or at least it has been for me) in terms of both speed and budget usage. 



There are a substantive number of people who swear by having Astra write out the plan and then giving that plan to Sol as a means of massive token savings, because Astra uses very few tokens to plan but TONS of tokens to execute on that plan, whereas Sol is dirt cheap in execution... 

I'll be honest, I do not trust Sol with that level of abstraction. I haven't really tried it, but I am extremely skeptical that Sol would be capable of following Astra's plans, especially without context (as capable as Sol is at its price point, it is still vastly inferior at reasoning compared to the latest models).

comments.author: Creepy-Doughnut-5054
comments.body: I generally do not like to be polite with ai as it then try harder to be sycophantic and subsequently sloppier and usually requiring more iterations. Instead I prefer to be strict, brief and mechanical, no bullshit and dancing around.

comments.author: SeasawPhilosopher
comments.body:
I actually think it’s better to move up to an even higher level of abstraction when working with AI. Don’t tell Codex/Astra you want a new specific weapon, that’s providing a solution and constraining things too much to prevent more interesting outcomes. Instead describe the problem. Maybe the game is boring with limited weapons, fights are mostly long ranged, and there’s a lack of balance. You can suggest a shotgun as a solution but the model should be allowed to solve a gameplay problem for you more openly. Also, suggest it use data to guide the process by examining the gameplay and existing weapons, level design, and also running bot simulations. Then if you do decide on a shotgun you can use these same data driven method to balance the cost, range, power, reload speed, etc.

The last generation of models were task rabbits, but the frontier models are general purpose problem solvers. If you still treat them as brain dead code monkeys you miss out on finding creative solutions to game design problems and developing a more interesting and cohesive game.

comments.author: OhGoodGames
comments.body:
"I am developing \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_. Please ask me 10-15 questions about every necessary and relevant system that needs to be built to achieve \_\_\_\_\_\_\_. Use my answers to create a design document that includes a roadmap, milestones, and implementation plan."

Then you just hand that off to Sol.

replies.author: AsparagusOk8818
replies.body:
Oh, that's an interesting idea. 

How has Sol been with the results, in your experience?

replies.author: OhGoodGames
replies.body:
Still testing. I used Astra to write the design document and do a lot of the foundation coding work. Typically Astra will have the foundation work set as one of its first milestones anyways. The past week i've been exclusively using sol to build on top of that and honestly haven't noticed much difference between the models, so im inclined to keep using Sol unless i get stuck. I do get the feeling that sol is worse for UI and layout work though. Like noticeably worse. 

I also use Claude Opus, so Claude might be filling in some gaps too, but I don't feel the need to run both Opus and Astra.

I'm building an ASCII rendering based engine. Video is too long to post but you can check my profile

replies.author: AsparagusOk8818
replies.body:
OMFG YOU ARE THE ASCII ENGINE PERSON

YOUR WORK IS FCKN AMAZING!

replies.author: OhGoodGames
replies.body:
lol thank you for the compliment. I have been keeping a close eye on my agents. Especially during testing (one of my agents was doing tests outside the city limits so the performance numbers weren't accurate). But this is exactly how I started my current project. I did also give Astra instructions to pursue the development of new ASCII rendering technology, explicitly telling it to create and test new tech.  and I have several test environments to test all that as well.

I also revised the design document 13 times before i handed it off and i believe it was 30+ pages. So this was not a one and done slopfest. Even now i'm testing all types of rendering techniques to achieve better clarity and performance. 

And I still update the design document regularly. If I land on a new idea, or change my mind about something i'll tell Sol to "Update the design document and audit it against the ideas we discussed" to see where we land on implementation.

I have actually made significant gains the past few days with Sol regarding the clairty of visuals and will be posting another video here soon. Once i reach a good stopping point.

replies.author: AsparagusOk8818
replies.body:
I saw that you had posted the other day about having to implement some 3D models for the project and being a bit disappointed... 

Just want to say, do not worry about it. Just have a go and see what happens, IMHO.   
  
Even if nothing comes of it and the engine turns out to not be practical, it's still just so fckn cool. That kind of raw experimentation within the medium isn't given enough appreciation, and is the kind of thing that can accomplish so much more than even the best purpose-driven game design because we're just over here iterating. You're over there innovating. 

We need both of those things.
